Paragraph 2: As they came in my direction, I put on my brightest and happiest smile. I wanted to make them know that I was really anxious to help them. To my relief, they smiled politely back at me when they saw my smile, and I could see their exhaustion in their eyes. I wanted to know what they, the homeless, were going through and I was desperate to know what I could do for them.【高分句型一】They nodded gratefully as I pushed my spoon into the pot and took a large spoonful and poured it into their bowls.（作者是怎么为无家可归的人施粥的）

paragraphs.text: Pasta and pizza were on everyone’s lunch menu in my native land of Italy. Everyone who had such a lunch was fair-skinned and spoke Italian. A few years later, as I stood in the lunch line with my kindergarten class in a school in Brooklyn, I realized things were no longer that simple. My classmates ranged from those kids with pale skin and large blue eyes to those with rich brown skin and dark hair. The food choices were almost as diverse as the students. In front of me was an array of foods I couldn’t even name in my native language. Fearing that I would pick out something awful, I desperately tried to ask the boy ahead of me for a recommendation. Unfortunately, between us stood the barrier of language.

Although my kindergarten experience feels like a century ago, the lessons I learned will stick in my mind forever. For the past three summers, I have worked in a government agency in New York. New immigrants much like the little girl in the lunch line flooded our office seeking help. I often had to be an interpreter for the Italian-speaking ones. As I served the role of vital communication link, I was reminded of my desperate struggle to converse before I learned English. I watched with great sympathy as elderly Italians tried to hold a conversation in Italian with people who did not speak the language. It suddenly became very clear to me how lucky I was to be fluent in two languages.

In New York, a multicultural city, students like me are blessed with a chance to work with a diverse population. In my English to Italian translations, I’ve learned about social programs that I didn’t know existed. This work expanded my mind in ways that are impossible inside the four walls of a classroom. Walking through the streets of Brooklyn today, I am no longer confused by this city’s sounds and smells. Instead, enjoy its diversity.

All around the world, there are small changes taking place. At the side of roads, behind school playgrounds and on all kinds of unloved pieces of land across towns and cities, tiny forests barely the size of tennis courts are appearing, making a great place for both wildlife and local people who may not normally have easy access to nature. This is the Tiny Forest movement, which aims to prove that the best things in life really do come in small packages.

Tiny forests were first pioneered as a concept in the 1970s by Dr Miyawaki, a Japanese botanist. As he went on to share his concept with others, the idea soon took off in India and other countries before eventually reaching Europe, where it became popular in places like France, Belgium and the Netherlands.

So how does it work? Louise Hartley, who is leading the Tiny Forest project in the UK, explains that the process begins by identifying areas in which a tiny forest could have the biggest influence. “We focus on urban areas where access to nature is often not that easy,” says Hartley. “We see it as a chance to try to break the growing disconnect between people and nature.”

In a Tiny Forest, there must be a minimum of 600 trees, and the trees are planted much closer together and without chemicals or fertilisers (肥料) . There are usually around 30 different kinds of all-native tree species (物种) . This variety, coupled with the fact that tiny forests grow up to ten times faster than standard forests, means they attract a rich abundance of wildlife. It’s also thought that these places could help reduce the risk of flooding, remove carbon from the atmosphere and fight climate change, as well as improving the mental health of those living locally.
Many people believe that working to the maximum is the secret to success, but research has found that moderation (适度) also gets results on the job.

In a study led by Ellen Langer of Harvard University, researchers asked people to translate sentences into a new made-up language. Subjects who practiced the language moderately beforehand made fewer errors than those who practiced extensively or not at all. High levels of knowledge can make people too attached to traditional ways of viewing problems across fields — the arts, sciences, and politics. High conscientiousness is related to lower job performance, especially in simple jobs where it doesn’t pay to be a perfectionist.

How long we stay on the clock and how we spend that time are under careful examination in many workplaces. The young banker who eats lunch at his desk is probably seen as a go-getter, while his colleagues who chat over a relaxed conference-room meal get dirty looks from the corner office. “People from cultures that value relationships more than ours does are shocked by the thought of eating alone in front of a computer”, says Art Markman, a professor of psychology at the University of Texas, Austin. Social interaction has been shown to lift mood (情绪) and get people thinking in new directions and in ways that could help improve any post-lunch effort.

Markman also promotes off-task time. “Part of being a good thinker is experiencing things that are seemingly unrelated to what you are working on at the moment but give you fresh ideas about your work,” he says. “Also, there is a lot of research showing that a positive mood leads to higher levels of productivity and creativity. So, when people do things to increase their life satisfaction, they also make themselves more effective at work.”

paragraphs.text: I have a drawer full of letters to Santa. Each year my children would write up their Christmas wish lists. They were polite requests for the latest game or toy. As the children got older, they would give Santa some hints (提示) on where to buy their presents. __31__ 1

Those letters taught my children a valuable lesson about writing: It has a purpose. Sometimes our purpose is to achieve something; other times may be to entertain, inform, or persuade. __32__ 2   And when writing doesn’t seem to have any purpose or get any kind of meaningful response, then it can be hard to get excited about doing it.

Christmas is a great time of year for children to communicate with others through writing. When children write for real audiences and real purposes, they can learn to choose their words accordingly. __33__ 3  You write “Dear Santa” because you don’t know him personally and you want to show him respect.

__34__ 4  Texting, online messaging, live chats while playing video games all mean that they are constantly producing written messages. However, because they are usually writing to family and friends, they use informal language most of the time.

There is nothing wrong with this kind of writing. It suits the audience and the purpose and gets the job done. __35__ 5   This type of writing won’t be rewarded by the school examiner, nor by a future employer or a potential client. The very best communicators are those who know how to adjust their language to match their audience.

假定你是李华，你校图书馆新设了小组学习室。请你给留学生同学Michael写邮件邀请他同去体验，内容包括：
（1）位置和开放时间；
（2）室内设施和功能。
（1）词数80左右；
（2）可适当增加细节，以使行文连贯。

I needed to do something in my community in order to complete the community service hours required to graduate from high school. Some of my friends had signed up to spend time at a soup kitchen, so I did, too. It seemed like a good thing to do.

I thought that we would just be passing out dinners to those in need, but I found out we would be doing everything from preparing to serving the dinner. We began preparing the food, from mixing salad dressing to separating frozen meat. Much still needed to be done before dinner was served, but already outside the building many homeless people were gathering. It wasn’t until a couple of hours later that we opened the doors and began serving dinner.

As the line of people came toward me, I got a little scared. I’d come face to face with the homeless: How should I act? How would they treat me? Would they hate me for having more than they did? While some of the people looked very friendly, some of them looked so dangerous. I didn’t have too much time to worry about it. I was assigned (分配) to serve the salad with the lady next to me. She smiled at me and said if I needed help, she’d be right there, which I found quite comforting.

I had never seen so many people wanting food. They were of all ages and nationalities. Most of them wore clothes that were torn and dirty. Some looked like they had totally given up on life, while others seemed to be making the best of the situation, smiling and joking. Some were better off than others, but they all needed a good meal and a warm place to eat. It saddened me to think of how many people there were who didn’t have a place to call home and the only food they got came from a soup kitchen.

group-zj-2022-jun-reading-a.overview: 记叙文。作者是一名来自意大利的移民女孩，回忆自己初到布鲁克林上幼儿园时因语言和文化差异而手足无措，长大后在纽约政府机构做暑期工担任意大利语翻译，帮助新移民，从而体会到掌握双语的幸运并学会欣赏这座多元文化城市的多样性。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按时间顺序展开：童年初到布鲁克林感受到人和食物的多样与语言障碍（第一段）→ 多年后做暑期工当翻译、由己及人体会双语之幸运（第二段）→ 在多元都市中成长、视野超越课堂、最终从困惑到欣赏多样性（第三段）。

paragraphs.summary: 作者对比意大利单一的午餐与人群，和布鲁克林幼儿园里肤色各异的同学、五花八门的食物，因不懂英语想求人推荐却受阻于语言障碍。
paragraphs.function: 开篇设景，通过今昔对比引出多样性主题，并埋下语言障碍这一伏笔。

paragraphs.summary: 作者讲述近三年暑假在纽约政府机构工作、为说意大利语的新移民当翻译，看到老年意大利人因语言不通而挣扎，由此回想自己当年的窘境，意识到自己精通双语何其幸运。
paragraphs.function: 由童年经历过渡到成年实践，借暑期工经历呼应开篇语言障碍，点出感悟。

paragraphs.summary: 作者总结在多元文化的纽约与多样人群共事的收获：通过翻译了解了原先不知道的社会项目，视野得到课堂内无法获得的拓展，如今走在布鲁克林街头不再困惑，而是享受这座城市的多样性。
paragraphs.function: 升华主题，揭示暑期工带来的视野拓展与心态转变，首尾呼应收束全文。

group-zj-2022-jun-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇说明文，介绍了在世界各地兴起的“微型森林”（Tiny Forest）运动：它的现状与意义、起源与传播、运作方式与目标，以及微型森林中树木的种植特点和生态价值。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按“现象引入—起源传播—运作目标—构成与价值”的逻辑展开：先描述微型森林正在各地悄然出现的现象，再追溯其概念起源与全球传播，接着借项目负责人之口说明运作方式与核心目标，最后说明微型森林的构成特点及其多重生态与健康效益。

paragraphs.summary: 在世界各地的路边、操场后和闲置土地上，网球场大小的微型森林正在出现，既造福野生动物也造福平时难以亲近自然的当地人。这就是“微型森林”运动，旨在证明生活中最美好的事物确实蕴含在小小的包装里。
paragraphs.function: 引入主题，以现象描述点出“微型森林”运动及其宗旨。

paragraphs.summary: 微型森林这一概念由日本植物学家宫胁博士于20世纪70年代首创，随后这一理念在印度等国流行，最终传到欧洲，在法国、比利时和荷兰等地颇受欢迎。
paragraphs.function: 追溯微型森林概念的起源与全球传播路径。

paragraphs.summary: 英国项目负责人Louise Hartley解释其运作方式：先确定微型森林能发挥最大影响的区域，重点关注亲近自然不易的城市地区，把它看作弥合人与自然日益疏离的机会。
paragraphs.function: 通过项目负责人之口说明运作方式，并点明项目目标。

paragraphs.summary: 微型森林至少有600棵树，种植得更密、不用化肥，通常约有30种全部为本土的树种；这种多样性加上其生长速度比普通森林快十倍，使其吸引大量野生动物，并有助于减少洪灾风险、固碳、应对气候变化以及改善当地居民的心理健康。
paragraphs.function: 说明微型森林的构成特点及其多重生态与健康价值。

group-zj-2022-jun-reading-c.overview: 本文为说明/议论性文章，主旨是：在职场上，凡事做到极致并非成功的唯一秘诀，适度（moderation）同样能带来好结果。文章先提出适度观点，再用哈佛研究证明适度练习效果最好，接着讨论午餐、社交互动对工作的积极影响，最后引用专家观点说明脱离任务的活动和积极情绪能提升工作效率与创造力。

discourseStructure.summary: 总—分结构。第一段提出中心论点（适度也能出成绩）；第二段用Langer的研究及相关发现为论点提供实验与事实支撑；第三段转向时间使用方式，指出社交化的午餐有益工作；第四段引用Markman观点，论证脱离任务的时间与积极情绪能提升效率和创造力，呼应并强化适度/平衡的主旨。

paragraphs.summary: 很多人认为全力以赴是成功的秘诀，但研究发现适度也能在工作中出成绩。
paragraphs.function: 引出全文中心论点：moderation 同样有效，奠定全文基调。

paragraphs.summary: Langer的研究显示，适度练习造句的人犯错最少；过高的知识水平会使人固守传统思路，过高的尽责性反而降低简单工作的表现。
paragraphs.function: 用实验证据和相关研究支撑'适度最优'的论点，反驳'越极致越好'。

paragraphs.summary: 工作时长与时间使用方式受到关注：在办公桌前独自吃午餐被视为拼命三郎，而轻松的会议室共餐却遭白眼；专家指出社交互动能提升情绪、激发新思路。
paragraphs.function: 由练习转入时间使用与社交，说明社交化用餐对工作有益，进一步支撑平衡/适度主张。

paragraphs.summary: Markman主张安排脱离任务的时间，认为体验看似无关的事物能带来新灵感，积极情绪能提高生产力和创造力，提升生活满意度也会让人工作更高效。
paragraphs.function: 引用专家观点收束全文，论证脱离任务的时间与积极情绪的价值，强化适度/平衡的主旨。

q-zj-2022-jun-029.questionFocus: 考查对末段内容的推断，重点把握'积极情绪—创造力'之间的关系。
q-zj-2022-jun-029.stemTranslationZh: 从最后一段可以推断出什么？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 好的思考者能够激励他人。

trap.claim: A good thinker is able to inspire other people.
trap.explanation: 末段说优秀思考者会去体验看似无关的事物以获得新灵感，是自己获得 fresh ideas，并未提到能'激励他人'(inspire other people)，原文未提及。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 与工作无关的经历是无用的。

trap.sourceQuote: Part of being a good thinker is experiencing things that are seemingly unrelated to what you are working on at the moment but give you fresh ideas about your work
trap.sourceHighlight: seemingly unrelated to what you are working on at the moment but give you fresh ideas about your work
trap.optionText: Experience unrelated to your job is useless.
trap.optionHighlight: Experience unrelated to your job is useless
trap.explanation: 原文强调看似与工作无关的经历恰恰能带来新灵感、是有益的；选项却说'无关的经历无用'(useless)，评价完全相反。

trapEvidence.quote: experiencing things that are seemingly unrelated to what you are working on at the moment but give you fresh ideas about your work

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 愉快的心情有助于造就富有创造力的头脑。

evidence.quote: there is a lot of research showing that a positive mood leads to higher levels of productivity and creativity

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 专注于所做之事能提高生产力。

trap.sourceText: a positive mood leads to higher levels of productivity and creativity
trap.optionText: Focusing on what you do raises productivity.
trap.relationNote: 选项借用原文 productivity（与 raises productivity 同词族）制造干扰，但原文说提高生产力靠的是'积极情绪'(positive mood)以及脱离任务的体验，而非'专注于所做之事'(Focusing on what you do)；末段恰恰提倡 off-task time，与'一味专注'方向相反。

trapEvidence.quote: a positive mood leads to higher levels of productivity and creativity

locationParaphrases.sourceText: A cheerful mood helps make a creative mind.
locationParaphrases.targetText: a positive mood leads to higher levels of productivity and creativity
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 A cheerful mood helps make a creative mind 是对原文 a positive mood leads to higher levels of ... creativity 的同义转述：cheerful mood 对应 positive mood，creative mind 对应 higher levels of creativity。

q-zj-2022-jun-030.questionFocus: 考查对全文主旨/作者主张的把握：文章倡导的是什么。

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 中庸/不走极端的工作习惯。

evidence.quote: Many people believe that working to the maximum is the secret to success, but research has found that moderation (适度) also gets results on the job.
Subjects who practiced the language moderately beforehand made fewer errors than those who practiced extensively or not at all.

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 工作与家庭之间的平衡。

trap.explanation: 文章谈的是工作中适度用力、安排脱离任务时间与社交，全文未涉及'家庭'(family)这一维度，工作—家庭平衡属原文未提及。

trap.sourceText: People from cultures that value relationships more than ours does
trap.relationNote: 选项借用原文 cultures（与 cultural 同词族）设钩，但原文只是用'更重视人际关系的文化'来说明社交化用餐的价值，并非倡导'长期文化传统'(Long-standing cultural traditions)，并不是文章主张。

trapEvidence.quote: People from cultures that value relationships more than ours does

trap.sourceQuote: Social interaction has been shown to lift mood (情绪) and get people thinking in new directions and in ways that could help improve any post-lunch effort.
trap.sourceHighlight: Social interaction has been shown to lift mood
trap.explanation: 原文提到社交互动能提升情绪、激发新思路，但这只是支撑'适度'主旨的一个分论点；把全文主张拔高概括为'营造工作环境的和谐'(Harmony in the work environment)超出了文章范围，偷换了主旨。

trapEvidence.quote: Social interaction has been shown to lift mood

locationParaphrases.targetText: research has found that moderation (适度) also gets results on the job
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 Middle-of-the-road work habits（中庸的工作习惯）是对全文主旨词 moderation（适度）的同义替换；首段 moderation also gets results on the job 与后文'适度练习效果最好''脱离任务时间有益'共同指向不走极端、适度行事的工作方式。
